Forman's acyclic matching CW theorem as applied to the nonempty simplicial face poset
correctness.rationale: A point within a unit edge can only witness centers whose minimum integer distance to the endpoints is at most one; the midpoint then witnesses all of them simultaneously. A vertex witness is contained in a witness from any incident edge. This proves the two row/column facet forms for closed intrinsic balls. Independently reconstructed the seed complexes from shortest distances in the graph subdivided at all midpoints. Reconstructed the pivot matching and checked the full oriented Hasse DAG, obtaining 18 and 30 facets, 477 and 2950 nonempty faces, 236 and 1466 pairs, and critical dimensions respectively one in degree 0 and four in degree 5; and one each in degrees 0 and 4 and sixteen in degree 5. Exact rational elimination on the original signed simplicial boundaries gave ranks (70,56,18) and (330,461,327) for d4,d5,d6, with b4=0,1 and b5=4,16. In the q=4 Morse CW model, b4(Q)=1 forces the entire map to the sole integral 4-cell to vanish. The 4-skeleton is S^4 and each 5-cell attaches by a degree-zero, hence nullhomotopic, map S^4→S^4. In q=3 the 5-cells attach to a point. Folding columns j>=4 to zero maps either facet form into a facet in the first four columns, extending the horizontal candidate by an arbitrary second column if necessary. Inclusion and fold compose to the identity, giving the asserted integral split homology at every q>=4. Replay: python3 /workspace/review_evidence/rook.py.
residual_risks: The replay establishes the two seed models; only the split summands, not the full higher-width homology or absence of torsion in the complementary summands, follow from the retraction.

These facts determine actual lowest-width structure not supplied by a comparison of graph diameters or by a mod-two rank alone.
